source: Homay (2026) A Deep Dive into Axiomatic Design Part I: Problem Formulation
finding: Position paper (14 pages, no experiments) says LLMs cannot reliably produce the essential first-level functional requirements (FRs) in axiomatic design. Chatbots can help with design parameters and derived FRs.
numbers: No measurement. Claim rests on ARC benchmark results and an LLM-abduction essay (cited, not re-run by the paper).
limits: Opinion, written 'at the time of writing'; no test of any model on FR formulation. Untested claim.
agent_relevance: Treat as a hypothesis: have the program, not the model, check FR independence. Do not trust the model to pick the top-level need set.
quote: LLMs perform well in induction and are increasingly capable of deductive reasoning, they still struggle with abduction

source: Homay (2026) A Deep Dive into Axiomatic Design Part I: Problem Formulation
finding: Paper claims essential FRs should be the same for any designer given the same needs and constraints. Wording an FR with a contingent solution (example: 'over electromagnetic waves') merges FRs and breaks independence, and LLMs can copy such bad formulations.
numbers: Worked example: 'receive/make a call' vs 'receive/make a call over electromagnetic waves'. No counts.
limits: Single worked example; asserted, not measured.
agent_relevance: Maps to a check in the schema: restate the problem solution-neutral before generating options; flag any requirement that names a mechanism.

source: Homay (2026) A Deep Dive into Axiomatic Design Part I: Problem Formulation
finding: Claims coupling at the top FR level propagates irreversibly down all later layers; changes in design parameters cannot change essential FRs (one-way causal structure).
numbers: Conceptual claim based on Suh's three books.
limits: Theory only; not tested with models or humans here.
agent_relevance: Supports fixing the problem statement early and checking it before any search over solutions.

source: Giordano, Consoloni, Losanno, Chiarello, Fantoni (2025) Decoding the grammar of design theory for LLMs: axiomatic design
finding: Builds the first expert-annotated dataset to test whether LLMs follow axiomatic-design concepts: 6,000 patent sentences marked for FR, DP and FR-DP relation (AXR) with Doer-Action-Receiver structure.
numbers: 6,000 sentences; 19,555 annotated concepts; 161 face-validity errors (0.8%); 1,200 sentences double-annotated by two experts. Sentence mix: 41.33% had no FR and no DP; 25.78% DP only or FR only; a few percent had full FR+DP+relation.
limits: Dataset paper: it does NOT yet test any LLM (that is listed as future work). Authors say prompting LLMs is unlikely to do this reliably.
agent_relevance: Shows FR vs DP is hard to identify even for experts, so a program cannot rely on a model's own FR/DP labels without checks.

source: Giordano, Consoloni, Losanno, Chiarello, Fantoni (2025) Decoding the grammar of design theory for LLMs: axiomatic design
finding: Inter-annotator agreement between two trained experts was only moderate for axiomatic concepts. F1 ranged about 0.52 to 0.80, with the simple Action entity highest (0.80) and relation concepts lowest (about 0.52 to 0.57).
numbers: Two annotators, 1,200 sentences. F1 values (rounded): 0.80, 0.68, 0.66, 0.66, 0.57, 0.55, 0.52 across seven concepts; the PDF table was garbled so concept-to-number mapping is only partly certain.
limits: Row labels lost in text extraction; only range and the Action=0.80 value are reliable. Authors compare simple clinical entity tasks at around 0.8.
agent_relevance: Human ceiling for 'is this an FR or a DP' is itself low; scoring a model against one gold label would be noisy.

source: Giordano, Consoloni, Losanno, Chiarello, Fantoni (2025) Decoding the grammar of design theory for LLMs: axiomatic design
finding: Review of prior NLP for axiomatic design: Chen 2008 verb-noun retrieval, Li and Tate 2010 SAO rules for patents, Akay and Kim 2020 GPT-2 synthetic data plus classifier for FR vs DP, Akay and Kim 2021 BERT question answering ('What is the aim?' then 'How does it do FR?'), Akay et al. 2023 chatbot for FR/DP extraction, Kwon 2024 BERT extraction.
numbers: Akay and Kim 2021 evaluated qualitatively on 88 FR-DP pairs from 11 paper abstracts; El Hassani 2024 FMEA used 100 failure modes.
limits: Secondary reading of other papers; numbers are as quoted by Giordano et al. Prior evaluations were small and qualitative.
agent_relevance: Older systems used the FR then DP question chain as a prompt scaffold, a simple two-step operator.

source: Consoloni, Giordano, Miaschi, Dell'Orletta, Fantoni (2026) Prompting or Fine-Tuning? Extracting FRs and DPs from Patents
finding: Abstract only (full text blocked). Fine-tuned encoder models beat prompted decoder-only LLMs at extracting FRs and DPs from the 6,000-sentence patent set.
numbers: Gap up to 0.1 F1 for sentence classification and up to 0.4 F1 for named-entity recognition. About 1,000 annotated examples were enough for fine-tuning to beat prompting.
limits: Abstract read through Crossref only; model names, prompts and exact scores not seen. SSRN preprint, may change.
agent_relevance: For FR/DP labelling, plain prompting is weak; a scaffold that only prompts will lose to a small trained classifier.

source: Akay and Kim (2020) Measuring functional independence in design with deep-learning language representation models
finding: Title and metadata only: first use of language-model embeddings to score functional independence (the independence axiom) between requirements.
numbers: No numbers seen.
limits: Full text blocked (403). Only title, authors and venue verified through Crossref; the description of method is inferred from the title.
agent_relevance: Closest prior to a model-scored independence check; worth reading in full before building one.

source: Akay, Yang, Kim (2021) Automating Design Requirement Extraction From Text With Deep Learning
finding: Abstract only: recursive question-answering system finds the top-level FR, then extracts further FRs. Compared to 75 human designers doing the same analysis on MEMS texts.
numbers: 75 human designers as comparison group; results not seen.
limits: Abstract via Crossref; PDF blocked (403).
agent_relevance: A recursive top-down extraction loop is an early example of axiomatic decomposition run by a model.

source: Jadhav and Barati Farimani (2024/2025) LLM Agent as a Mechanical Designer
finding: LLM plus finite-element check designs 2D truss structures in a propose, evaluate, refine loop. No axiomatic design is used, but it is an LLM agent doing design with a code-based checker. It reached feasible designs and chose when to stop.
numbers: Models GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1-mini; temperatures 0.5, 1.0, 1.2; 10 independent runs per setting; up to 10 attempts per generation; two tasks with variations.
limits: Not axiomatic design. Authors' own benchmark, 2D trusses only. Most results are in plots rather than tables.
agent_relevance: Pattern matches our schema: model proposes, program checks. Shows it works for structured design, but not an independence test.

source: Jadhav and Barati Farimani (2024/2025) LLM Agent as a Mechanical Designer
finding: Smaller model did a little better at constraint satisfaction with fewer iterations; lower temperature gave more consistent structure performance and higher success rates.
numbers: GPT-4.1-mini vs GPT-4.1; temps 0.5 vs 1.0 vs 1.2; success rate = successful structures divided by attempts, 10 runs each.
limits: Differences described as marginal; exact success rates are in figures I could not read as numbers.
agent_relevance: Lower temperature for the checked-propose step looks safer; a bigger model is not automatically better.

source: Jadhav and Barati Farimani (2024/2025) LLM Agent as a Mechanical Designer
finding: Against NSGA-II, the LLM agent converged faster and needed fewer FEM evaluations in a discrete space with dynamic node creation. NSGA-II failed to find feasible trusses when node bounds were removed, even with 100,000 evaluations. Bayesian optimisation and ground-structure methods also failed for this setup.
numbers: NSGA-II: 1000 generations x population 100 = 100,000 FEM evaluations with no feasible result when unbounded; fair comparison runs used 500 generations x 100.
limits: Authors' baselines; comparison fair only in the bounded setting. One problem family.
agent_relevance: A model used as a search proposer can beat classic search in loosely bounded spaces, when a code check scores each proposal.

source: Auto-DSM: Using a LLM to generate a Design Structure Matrix (2023)
finding: Auto-DSM workflow (gpt-3.5-turbo, temperature 0, LangChain) filled a published diesel-engine design structure matrix (the dependency matrix that axiomatic design's design matrix resembles) from text sources. It reproduced 357 of 462 entries.
numbers: 357/462 = 77.3% of published entries reproduced. Correctness (symmetric links) ranged 40.0% to 82.6% by input source: handbook [2] 82.6%, handbook [1] 54.5%, YouTube comments [3] 40.0%; pooled sources 70.2% and 72.3%.
limits: One engine case, one old model, one source set. Correctness measures symmetry not truth. Completeness (non-'do not know' share) ran 98.7% to 100% and did not track correctness.
agent_relevance: Model-filled dependency matrices depend heavily on the source text. A 'do not know' option exists but was barely used (completeness near 100%), so the model overcommits.

source: Auto-DSM: Using a LLM to generate a Design Structure Matrix (2023)
finding: Calling ChatGPT directly (without the workflow's component step) gave correctness 66.7% to 85.7%, more stable than Auto-DSM but not clearly better, and lower completeness in every setting.
numbers: Direct ChatGPT correctness 66.7 to 85.7% vs Auto-DSM 40 to 82.6%; same prompts; ChatGPT found 20 engine components.
limits: Authors call it inconclusive; small DSMs (4 to 15 components).
agent_relevance: The scaffold did not clearly improve accuracy; it improved coverage and component boundaries only.

source: Jiang, Xie, Luo (2024/2025) LLMs for Combinatorial Optimization of Design Structure Matrix
finding: LLM loop (Claude-3.5-Sonnet) re-orders a DSM to cut feedback (the same goal as making a design matrix triangular, i.e. decoupled). It converged faster than a genetic algorithm and beat five deterministic ranking methods across four cases.
numbers: 10 runs per method, 20 iterations, solution pool 5 best plus 5 random; GA given the same count of unique solutions. Four cases incl. automobile brake system (14 nodes). Backbones tested: Claude-3.5-Sonnet best, Llama3-70B second, plus Mixtral-8x7B and GPT-4-Turbo.
limits: Small DSMs (about 14 nodes or fewer in the cases shown). 'Multiple orders of magnitude faster' is the authors' claim measured in unique solutions explored.
agent_relevance: Direct analogue of a code-checked loop that removes coupling. The model proposes orderings, code scores them.

source: Jiang, Xie, Luo (2024/2025) LLMs for Combinatorial Optimization of Design Structure Matrix
finding: Adding domain knowledge about what each node is improved solution quality for every backbone tested in sequencing.
numbers: Ablation with and without knowledge, single-trial, 5-trial and 20-trial runs, four backbones.
limits: Later work (Jiang and Luo 2026) found the opposite for modularization.
agent_relevance: Semantic hints help when the goal is about process logic.

source: Jiang and Luo (2026) Design Structure Matrix Modularization with LLMs
finding: Extends the loop to modularization (grouping DSM elements). Claude-Sonnet-4.6 reached the simulated-annealing reference cost in 30 iterations. On the largest case (Helicopter, 19 elements) all 10 runs matched the reference cost (1371).
numbers: 3 models (Claude-Sonnet-4.6, GPT-5.2, Qwen-3.5-Plus) x 5 cases x 10 trials x 30 iterations, temperature 1.0. Claude within 1.3% of reference on three mid cases. GPT and Qwen had higher run-to-run variance.
limits: Five small cases; single prompt design; one task type (clustering).
agent_relevance: Model choice matters a lot for stability; the strongest model was clearly more reliable.

source: Jiang and Luo (2026) Design Structure Matrix Modularization with LLMs
finding: Knowledge paradox: domain knowledge hurt on bigger problems. For Claude, giving element meanings added a 5.4% cost gap on Heat Exchanger and 3.6% on Helicopter (k=1: zero of 10 runs matched reference; k=0: 10 of 10). It helped only slightly on UCAV (gap 0.9% vs 2.0%).
numbers: Gap% vs SA reference, 10 runs each, Claude-Sonnet-4.6. GPT and Qwen gained early from knowledge but the gain faded.
limits: Authors' semantic-alignment hypothesis is a guess, untested. Five cases.
agent_relevance: When the objective is purely structural, hints about what things mean can mislead. Keep the checked score as judge and do not feed in semantic labels by default.

source: Jiang and Luo (2026) Design Structure Matrix Modularization with LLMs
finding: Prompt ablations: keeping both best and random earlier solutions beats best-only or random-only; removing the cost formula from the prompt changed nothing; removing edge direction was the most damaging change.
numbers: UCAV case, Claude, k=1, 30 iterations, 10 runs. Directed edge list, adjacency matrix and plain-language description all ended similar; undirected list clearly worse.
limits: One case for ablations.
agent_relevance: The model ranks by examples, not by formula. Show scored candidates, keep direction information.

source: Garcia Alarcia and Golkar (2024) Optimizing token usage on LLM conversations using the DSM
finding: Uses DSM clustering and sequencing to split a spacecraft-design chat into pieces with a token budget, so output limits are not exceeded. A method moved from design theory into LLM conversation management.
numbers: Mistral 7B local; initial budget left about 1,400 output tokens lost; after DSM clustering the budget improved (single-context figure about 11,989 in the table).
limits: Single worked example, no human or model quality scores, only token counting; table numbers partly unreadable after text extraction.
agent_relevance: Splitting work by dependency strength is a cheap way to plan context windows and agent sub-tasks (independent sub-tasks together).

source: Jiang, Xie, Luo (2026) LLMs for DSM sequencing as combinatorial optimization, Research in Engineering Design
finding: Journal version of the sequencing work (abstract only): faster convergence and better solutions than stochastic and deterministic baselines; domain knowledge helps regardless of backbone.
numbers: No new numbers seen.
limits: Abstract via Crossref.
agent_relevance: Same as arXiv version; cite once.

source: Joshi et al. (2026) Enterprise AI System Design framework combining Axiomatic Design
finding: Abstract only: applies Suh's independence and information axioms to agentic enterprise AI design; claims AD-constrained design cut functional coupling and design iterations in three case studies.
numbers: Reported: coupling down 34.2% (p<.01), iterations down 41%, accessibility compliance 91.7% vs 54.2%, latency down 22%, three cases.
limits: Self-reported on SSRN preprint with the framework author as source; unverified, no baseline detail, no peer review. Treat with strong doubt.
agent_relevance: Only claimed use of the independence axiom inside an agent system design; not verified.

source: AI-assisted migration framework: RM-ODP, LLMs and DSM (arXiv 2608.23146, 2026)
finding: Pipeline: LLM names workflow components and their dependencies, DSM analysis refines the structure, LLM writes the components. Two legacy science apps converted with function preserved.
numbers: Two applications; no quantitative results in the abstract; 8 pages, 5 tables.
limits: Only the abstract page was read. Coupling is not measured by name. Authors not recorded.
agent_relevance: Example of a dependency-matrix check inside an LLM code-generation loop.

source: Li, Suh, Xu, Song (2022) Extenics-enhanced axiomatic design procedure for AI applications
finding: Abstract only: adds Extenics representation and a computer-aided step-by-step fill-in tool to axiomatic design; says novices find AD hard to apply. Example: corn harvester header.
numbers: One example, no numbers.
limits: Not an LLM; computer-aided rule-based system. Abstract via Crossref.
agent_relevance: Old tool pattern: a form that walks the designer through FR to DP mapping.

source: Lee et al. (2025) Reasoning abilities of LLMs: analysis on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus; cited by Homay
finding: Cited by Homay as evidence that top LLMs trail humans on abstraction; not opened by me.
numbers: No numbers seen.
limits: Only seen as a citation in Homay 2026.
agent_relevance: Weak indirect link: Homay's claim about abstraction rests on this and on a DeepMind essay.
